name: Introduction to Actuarial Mathematics and Risk Analytics
description:
This course provides an introductory exposure to actuarial mathematics and modern risk analytics, emphasizing intuition, conceptual clarity, and practical insight, with a focus on real-world relevance and applications rather than mathematical rigour.The course is intended to be more application-oriented.
It covers fundamental topics such as survival models, life tables, and the valuation of life insurance and annuity products, along with brief extensions to pension systems, multi-state models, and population-based frameworks. The course also introduces non-life insurance models, including frequency–severity approaches, and basic quantitative risk measures such as Value-at-Risk (VaR) and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR). Dependence modeling using copulas and extreme value theory for tail risk—are included at a basic conceptual level only to provide exposure to modern tools in risk assessment.
A strong emphasis is placed on computational implementation and applications through project-based activities, enabling students to perform actuarial analysis in simulated or realistic scenarios.
